title: Senior Program Manager, Consumer Device Safety Operations
description:
About the Team

At OpenAI, the User Safety & Risk Operations (USRO) team helps protect our products and users from abuse, fraud, safety risks, and other forms of misuse. We operate at the front line of real-world safety and risk management, translating user and operational signals into timely decisions, effective interventions, and improvements to our systems.

This role sits on a team focused on building operational capacity for new, ambiguous, and fast-moving company priorities. The team defines what needs to be built, creates the operating model to support it, and works with partner teams to make the work scalable and durable over time.

About the Role

We are looking for a senior program manager to build the safety, quality, and risk operations supporting a new category of consumer devices. You will translate ambiguous product risks and evolving requirements into practical operating models, workflows, escalation paths, launch-readiness plans, and cross-functional decision-making. This is a foundational role: the systems you build will shape how OpenAI launches, monitors, and improves a new category of consumer devices safely at scale.

You will help establish how potential safety incidents, product-quality concerns, sensitive customer escalations, privacy-sensitive issues, and other emerging device risks are identified, investigated, resolved, and incorporated into product and operational improvements. You will turn incomplete requirements into practical workflows, decision rights, launch plans, quality controls, measurement, and durable ownership.

The role centers on program building, operational judgment, and execution. We welcome candidates from product safety, quality assurance, regulatory operations, technical program management, healthcare, medical devices, aerospace, consumer technology, and other environments involving complex products or regulated risks. Direct consumer-hardware experience is helpful but not required.

The strongest candidates learn unfamiliar technical domains quickly, ask sharp questions, and translate product, engineering, quality, regulatory, policy, legal, and user needs into operations that work in practice.

Location / work model: San Francisco, CA; hybrid, 3 days/week in-office.

Please note: This role may involve exposure to sensitive or concerning material. Strong discretion, judgment, and resilience are essential.

In This Role, You Will

  • Lead strategic operational builds for device-safety and product-quality priorities from problem statement to implemented operating model, including scope, owners, milestones, risks, success measures, and execution cadence.

  • Define intake, severity criteria, decision rights, evidence requirements, escalation paths, response standards, closure criteria, and post-incident learning for high-risk cases.

  • Translate product, engineering, quality, regulatory, legal, privacy, policy, support, and operational requirements into practical workflows, clear ownership, playbooks, and measurable operating standards.

  • Build launch-readiness plans, training, quality controls, reporting, monitoring, and early-life response mechanisms.

  • Coordinate across Product, Hardware and Software Engineering, Product Safety, Product Quality, Legal, Privacy, Product Policy, Support, Logistics, vendors, and USRO to resolve dependencies and keep critical work moving. Partner with fraud, privacy, legal, and other specialized teams when device-related issues require their expertise.

  • Use operational data, dashboards, customer signals, product telemetry, case-management systems, AI tools, and qualitative evidence to investigate issues, measure performance, identify patterns, and improve workflows.

  • Drive critical escalations and cross-functional decisions to closure with clear context, accountable owners, documented decisions, and durable follow-through.

  • Create the mechanisms that make complex programs run well, including roadmaps, decision logs, risk registers, operating reviews, status updates, and executive communication.

  • Identify where AI tools, automation, lightweight systems, or simpler workflows can improve speed, consistency, investigation, and quality while preserving appropriate human judgment.

  • Stand up priority workflows, operate them through launch and stabilization, and transition mature capabilities into durable homes across USRO and partner teams.

You Might Thrive in This Role If You

  • Have 8+ years of experience in program management, technical program management, product operations, product safety, quality assurance, regulatory operations, incident management, healthcare operations, or another complex, high-accountability operational field.

  • Are technically and analytically fluent enough to reason about data flows, telemetry, logs, dashboards, access controls, case systems, automation, and failure modes, even if you are not writing production code.

  • Have a track record of taking complex, ambiguous, and unstructured work from problem framing through product launch, operational readiness, and scaled operation.

  • Can create clarity across many moving pieces without losing the few decisions, risks, and dependencies that matter most.

  • Have sound judgment in high-severity or sensitive situations and can make practical, risk-based decisions with incomplete information.

  • Build trust and drive alignment across teams without direct authority while keeping ownership, accountability, and escalation paths clear.

  • Communicate clearly and directly with technical, operational, legal, policy, and executive audiences, especially when tradeoffs are sensitive or evidence is incomplete.

  • Are highly practical and willing to build and run the first version of a workflow, learn from real cases, and improve the system over time.

  • Operate calmly in a fast-moving environment, learn new domains quickly, and adjust priorities without losing rigor or follow-through.

Nice to Have

  • Experience with consumer hardware, connected devices, medical devices, healthcare technology, aerospace, robotics, mobility, wearables, or another technically complex or regulated physical product.

  • Experience with device launches, product quality, field incidents, safety-sensitive customer escalations, repairs, warranty, returns, reverse logistics, or privacy-sensitive sensor and diagnostic data.

  • A technical degree or equivalent experience partnering closely with hardware, software, data, or systems engineering teams.

  • Experience with vendor operations, quality-assurance programs, regulated-product operations, incident response, workflow automation, or AI-assisted operations.

title: Commissioning Project Lead, Data Center Delivery
description:
About the Team

OpenAI’s Industrial Compute organization is building the infrastructure required to support the next generation of frontier AI systems. Through a combination of strategic partnerships and self-built data center campuses, we are scaling the power, cooling, electrical, mechanical, and controls infrastructure needed to deliver compute at unprecedented scale.

The Commissioning organization is responsible for ensuring this infrastructure is safely tested, validated, integrated, and transitioned into reliable operations. For our self-build campuses, the team operates through a hybrid delivery model: OpenAI provides commissioning leadership, discipline ownership, governance, and project integration, while commissioning partners provide field and test engineering capacity to support inspections, startup, testing, and turnover.

About the Role

We are seeking a Commissioning Project Lead to own the commissioning strategy and execution for a large-scale, self-build data center project.

You will lead the overall commissioning program from early construction planning through startup, functional testing, integrated systems testing, and final turnover. You will establish the commissioning execution plan, integrate commissioning activities into the master project schedule, coordinate multidisciplinary readiness, and lead the vendor commissioning partners providing field and test engineering capacity.

This role serves as the primary commissioning interface to project leadership, construction management, contractors, equipment vendors, operations, and commissioning partners. You will be responsible for creating clarity across organizations, identifying readiness and schedule risks early, and ensuring the facility progresses through testing and turnover against clearly defined acceptance criteria.

The role will initially support planning and coordination in a hybrid capacity and transition to full-time onsite presence as construction, inspections, startup, testing, and turnover become active.

Key Responsibilities

  • Own the project commissioning strategy and execution plan, including scope, governance, acceptance criteria, responsibilities, sequencing, and escalation paths.

  • Lead the hybrid OpenAI and commissioning-partner delivery model, establishing clear RACI ownership, staffing requirements, performance expectations, and issue-management processes.

  • Lead commissioning coordination across construction management, contractors, design teams, equipment vendors, operations stakeholders, and field/test engineering teams.

  • Professional credentials such as a PE license, QCxP, CxA, BCxP, CCP, PMP, or other relevant commissioning, engineering, construction, or project management certification are preferred.

title: GRC Program Manager, Audit & Controls
description:
About the Team

OpenAI’s Governance, Risk, and Compliance team helps ensure security and privacy are grounded in how our products and systems actually operate. Assurance Operations partners with Security, Engineering, Infrastructure, Product, Privacy, and Legal to make controls provable, risk decisions explicit, and audit readiness a result of well-designed systems.

About the Role

We are hiring a technical, product-minded GRC builder who can own consequential audits while improving the control and evidence systems behind them. You will build a reusable common control framework, use Codex to automate assurance work, validate changing system scope, and turn repeated audit friction into measurable improvements. We are looking for someone who questions inherited assumptions, solves novel problems creatively, works closely with engineers, and makes the next audit easier by improving the underlying system.

You’ll be responsible for:

  • Lead external, internal, customer, and certification audit work from scoping through evidence review, fieldwork, remediation, and closeout.

  • Build a common control framework linking risk, control intent, implementation, owner, system, environment, evidence, and applicable frameworks.

  • Validate actual scope and ownership instead of assuming last year's controls, product boundaries, or evidence remain accurate.

  • Use Codex to build and test evidence checks, control mappings, request triage, owner workflows, monitoring, and remediation reporting.

  • Partner with engineers on cloud architecture, identity, logging, data flows, software changes, vulnerabilities, and control effectiveness.

  • Design maintainable, permission-aware tools that preserve source provenance, human review, and evidence integrity.

  • Reduce repeated requests and operational burden for control owners through measurable workflow improvements.

  • Define roadmaps, decision rights, milestones, success metrics, and clear cross-functional escalations.

We’re looking for someone with:

  • Direct ownership of meaningful audit, security, customer-assurance, or regulatory outcomes.

  • Practical knowledge of control design, evidence, testing, operating effectiveness, and remediation.

  • Technical fluency across cloud systems, identity, logging, APIs, data flows, and system boundaries.

  • Ability to use Codex or comparable AI-assisted development tools to build, run, inspect, and test a working solution.

  • Experience using code, SQL, APIs, structured data, automation, or data workflows to solve an operational problem.

  • Ability to design reusable cross-framework controls without erasing framework-specific test and evidence requirements.

  • First-principles curiosity, creative problem solving, intellectual humility, and the ability to update when facts change.

HighLevel is an AI-powered business operating system that gives agencies, entrepreneurs, and SMBs the infrastructure to build, automate, and scale. Today, HighLevel supports SMBs across 150+ countries, fueling community-driven growth rooted in real customer outcomes.

To date, businesses operating on HighLevel have generated over $7 billion in ecosystem value. By centralizing conversations, automation, intelligence, and customer operations into one system, we help businesses move faster, reduce complexity, and execute efficiently.

Behind the platform, HighLevel powers more than 4 billion API hits and 2.5 billion message events daily, with 250 terabytes of distributed data, 250+ microservices, and over 1 million domain names supported. The architecture is built for performance, resilience, and long-term scalability.

Our people

With over 2,000 team members across 10+ countries, HighLevel operates as a global, remote-first organization built for speed and ownership. We value initiative, clarity and execution, creating space for ambitious people to build systems that support millions of businesses worldwide. Here, innovation thrives, ideas are celebrated and people come first, no matter where they call home.

Our impact

Every month, HighLevel enables more than 1.5 billion messages, 200 million leads, and 20 million conversations for more than 1 million businesses. Behind those numbers are agencies, entrepreneurs, and SMBs building independence, expanding opportunity, and creating measurable impact. We’re proud to be a part of that.
Learn more about us on our YouTube Channel or Blog Posts

Why This Role Exists

Voice is one of the highest-intent customer interaction channels for SMBs. Missed calls, delayed follow-ups, poor qualification, inconsistent appointment booking, and manual outbound outreach directly translate into lost revenue for local businesses and agencies.

HighLevel’s VoiceAI product is designed to change that.

VoiceAI enables businesses to deploy AI-powered voice agents that can answer inbound calls, hold natural conversations, collect customer information, book appointments, trigger workflows, send post-call summaries, and support both phone-based and browser-based voice experiences. VoiceAI also supports outbound calling from workflows for use cases like lead follow-up, appointment outreach, prospect engagement, and reactivation campaigns.

The Staff Product Manager – VoiceAI will own the strategy, execution, and quality bar for one of HighLevel’s most important AI products. This role sits at the intersection of AI agents, telephony, CRM, workflow automation, knowledge retrieval, compliance, analytics, and user experience.

You will be expected to deeply understand agencies, local businesses, call-heavy industries, and the real operational jobs that VoiceAI must perform: answer calls, qualify leads, route conversations, book appointments, follow up, summarize outcomes, and help businesses scale without adding headcount.

This is not a generic AI PM role. This is a hands-on, technically fluent, customer-obsessed product leadership role for someone who can build a reliable, scalable, commercially meaningful AI voice product inside a complex, high-volume SaaS platform.

Strategic Priorities

  • Make VoiceAI the default AI receptionist for SMBs: Build a product that reliably handles inbound calls, understands caller intent, answers questions, captures lead information, books appointments, and escalates when needed.

  • Scale outbound VoiceAI responsibly: Build workflow-driven outbound calling for lead follow-up, appointment reminders, reactivation, and prospect engagement while respecting platform limits, consent requirements, call quality, and compliance obligations. HighLevel’s current outbound VoiceAI supports workflow-based calls, up to 1,000 outbound VoiceAI calls per location per day, and time-zone-based scheduling between 8 AM and 8 PM based on the contact’s phone-number timezone.

  • Improve agent setup and time-to-value: Simplify agent creation, phone number assignment, prompt configuration, knowledge base selection, working hours, call actions, testing, and deployment so agencies can launch high-quality VoiceAI agents for clients quickly.

  • Drive call quality, reliability, and trust: Improve latency, interruption handling, speech recognition, natural conversation quality, escalation logic, call summaries, transcripts, recordings, and post-call workflows.

  • Deepen CRM and workflow integration: Ensure VoiceAI can update contact records, trigger workflows, generate summaries, collect structured fields, and feed downstream automation. VoiceAI currently supports post-call workflow triggers, email notifications, call summaries, contact information, transcripts, and actions taken.

  • Build VoiceAI as a platform capability: Advance public APIs, webhooks, call logs, agent configuration APIs, action APIs, voice catalog APIs, and developer-facing extensibility so agencies and developers can build repeatable voice agent solutions at scale.

Role Summary
As the Sr. Product Manager for Commerce Operations, you will own the operational backbone of HighLevel's commerce platform - the interconnected systems that govern how orders are created, tracked, and fulfilled; how subscriptions run across their full lifecycle; how transactions are recorded and reconciled; and how inventory, taxation, coupons, and gift cards function reliably at scale. You will also lead the build of HighLevel's internal accounting layer and design the integration surface for users who operate with third-party accounting tools — positioning commerce operations as both the authoritative source of financial truth and an open, compatible platform.

What You'll Do

● Own the Commerce Operations Roadmap: Define and drive the end-to-end product vision across HighLevel's full operations surface - Orders, Subscriptions, Transactions, Inventory, Fulfillment, Taxation, Coupons, and Gift Cards — ensuring each domain is built as a composable, reliable primitive that serves the platform as a whole.

● Build the Subscription Lifecycle: Own how plans, entitlements, renewals, upgrades, downgrades, pauses, and dunning flows work across the platform - building subscription management that handles the full complexity of real SMB billing, from simple recurring charges to tiered, usage-based, and trial-gated plans.

● Define the Ledger & Internal Accounting Layer: Lead the product definition and build of HighLevel's internal accounting layer — the authoritative system of record for every money-in and money-out event - designed from day one as the foundation for embedded accounting that keeps businesses running their books inside HighLevel.

● Enable Third-Party Accounting Compatibility: Design the integration surface that allows users who prefer external accounting software to sync HighLevel commerce data seamlessly - ensuring field mapping accuracy, reconciliation reliability, and a sync experience that requires zero manual intervention.

● Own Order Management & Fulfillment: Define how orders are created, modified, fulfilled, partially fulfilled, returned, and cancelled - building the state machine and merchant-facing workflows that make order operations reliable across every commerce surface, from storefronts to invoices to subscriptions.

● Build for Variable Granularity: Ensure every operational entity - order, fulfillment event, invoice, subscription, payment — is optional and composable. A business running on invoices alone and a business running a full order-fulfillment-invoice-payment chain must both be fully supported, with frictionless paths between granularity levels.

● Lead Inventory Management: Define the inventory layer - stock levels, reservations, adjustments, multi-location support, and low-stock signals - ensuring the platform correctly tracks physical goods across the full commerce lifecycle and exposes inventory state to every consuming surface.

● Shape Taxation & Compliance Infrastructure: Own the product strategy for tax calculation, tax code mapping, and compliance — across transaction types and geographies - ensuring HighLevel handles tax obligations correctly as merchants operate in multiple regions and as the platform expands internationally.

● Define Coupons, Promotions & Gift Cards: Build the discount and gift card infrastructure - coupon creation and validation, promotion rules, gift card issuance and redemption, balance tracking - ensuring these tools are expressive enough for merchant needs while enforcing correct financial accounting at every step.

● Own the Developer & Marketplace API Surface: Define and own the public API layer that external developers, agencies, and marketplace partners consume - ensuring commerce operations APIs are well-designed, stable, versioned, and expressive enough to support the full range of third-party integration and build use cases.

● Drive Cross-Functional Platform Alignment: Collaborate with the PIM, Documents, Onboarding, and Payments teams to ensure the operations layer exposes the primitives they depend on - and that operational events such as order placement, invoice issuance, and subscription renewal trigger the correct downstream behaviors reliably and consistently.

What We're Looking For

● 7+ Years of PM Experience: Proven track record in platform or infrastructure product management at high-growth SaaS companies, with significant exposure to transactional or financial systems.

● Commerce Operations Depth: Deep familiarity with order management, subscription billing, inventory, fulfillment, and transaction or ledger systems - understanding both the underlying data models and the merchant workflows built on top of them.

● Financial Systems Fluency: Comfort reasoning about ledger mechanics, double-entry accounting concepts, reconciliation requirements, and the data integrity standards of systems that carry financial truth for real businesses.

● API & Developer Platform Thinking: Experience building and owning public APIs consumed by external developers — with a strong grasp of contract design, versioning strategies, stability guarantees, and what makes a developer experience genuinely good.

● Platform-First Mindset: Demonstrated ability to design products as shared infrastructure - defining clear contracts, managing internal teams as stakeholders, and consistently prioritizing long-term extensibility over short-term feature velocity.

● Bias for Ownership: Comfortable holding the thread across a broad, interconnected domain without letting complexity become an excuse for slow decisions. Sets direction and drives execution independently.

What you'll get

● Strategic Centrality: Own the operational core that every other commerce surface depends on - a role with platform-wide impact, visibility across every team building on HighLevel's commerce infrastructure, and a direct line to the company's system-of-record ambition.

● High Ownership, Low Bureaucracy: Join an already-assembled engineering and design team and take full ownership of a mission-critical layer, with the autonomy to define the roadmap and drive execution at the pace HighLevel operates.

● Scale: Build the operational infrastructure that powers commerce for over a million businesses across 150+ countries, and define the accounting and developer API layer that will shape how HighLevel's commerce ecosystem grows over the next decade.

title: Product Lead, Infrastructure
description:
About Supabase


Supabase is the open-source Postgres development platform that 10M+ developers and thousands of enterprises depend on every day. Database, Auth, Storage, Edge Functions, Realtime and Vector Search all run on one platform: the same compute, the same disks, the same network and control plane, in every region we operate.

Supabase's hardest problems live in that platform. Millions of databases, growth that compounds every quarter, and a customer base running from a developer on a free project to a regulated enterprise routing traffic through PrivateLink. Reliability, capacity, cost and the enterprise features that close deals all come back to the same primitives. We're hiring a Product Lead to own them.

About the role

You own the platform primitives every Supabase product runs on: compute, disks, networking, the API gateway, capacity and regions. You own the enterprise surfaces built on top of them too, including read replicas, custom domains, PrivateLink and Bring Your Own Cloud. You report to the Head of Product and set direction for the whole area alongside the leads for our other product lines. You're the only product person on the platform today, and the team grows under you as the area does.

What you'll be responsible for:

  • You talk to customers across the full spectrum. Developers running a single small project, growing startups whose bill is mostly compute and disk, enterprises walking through a network architecture review, and partners building on top of Supabase.

  • You own the problem statement and requirements behind every platform bet. You define what we're building and why before engineering starts, name the cost, capacity and reliability constraints, and keep that clarity current through execution.

  • You decide what gets built, what gets deferred, and what gets cut. Every quarter you're choosing between enterprise unlocks that open new markets, cost and performance wins for the long tail of projects, and net-new capabilities that change what Supabase can run. The priorities are yours, and so is defending them.

  • You own reliability as a product surface. You set service levels that track what customers experience, hold teams to them, and show customers what it takes to run millions of databases.

  • You define how each launch is measured before it ships. The metric, the threshold and the read afterwards are yours: whether a launch moved enterprise deal velocity, project economics, or platform reliability.

  • You keep engineering, design and leadership aligned. The platform touches every other Supabase product, every region and every customer tier. You write down what's coming, why, and in what order, and you surface dependencies before they become blockers.

You might be a good fit if you:

  • Have 8+ years of product management experience on developer tools, or are an ex-founder who has built in this space. You're technical enough to read an architecture doc and follow a design discussion.

  • Have shipped cloud infrastructure as a product. You've owned at least one of compute, networking, storage, or multi-region and multi-tenant systems at a cloud, infrastructure or PaaS company, as the owner rather than a neighbouring team. You can judge the tradeoffs: instance sizing and capacity, disk and storage economics, scale-to-zero versus always-on, single-tenant versus shared, and the distance between "works in one region" and "works in twenty." Familiarity with how enterprises buy infrastructure (PrivateLink, BYOC, procurement) is a bonus.

  • Have grown with an infrastructure product. You've owned infrastructure small enough to hold in your head, and stayed with it until capacity, regions and cost became the real constraints.

  • Are biased toward speed. You'd rather ship something imperfect and learn from it.

  • Build with what you own. You stand up a read replica, put a custom domain in front of a project, terminate traffic through PrivateLink, deploy onto BYOC. You develop opinions through first-hand use.

  • Use AI to move faster. You lean on AI for the slow parts of the job (research, drafting, synthesising feedback) so you spend more time on judgment calls.

  • Work async by default. We're fully remote. You make decisions in writing and move work forward without meetings.

What We Offer

  • Fully Remote

    We hire globally. We believe you can do your best work from anywhere. There are no Supabase offices, but we provide a WeWork membership or co-working allowance you can use anywhere in the world.

  • ESOP

    Every team member receives ESOP (equity ownership) in the company. We want everyone to share in the upside of what we’re building together.

  • Tech Allowance

    Use this budget to set up your ideal work environment—laptop, monitor, headphones, or whatever helps you do your best work.

  • Health Benefits

    Supabase covers 100% of health insurance for employees and 80% for dependents, wherever you are. Your wellbeing and your family’s health are important to us.

  • Annual Off-Sites

    Once a year, the entire company gathers in a new city for a week of connection, collaboration, and fun. It’s a highlight of our year.

  • Flexible Work

    We operate asynchronously and trust you to manage your own time. You know what needs to be done and when.

  • Professional Development

    Every team member receives an annual education allowance to spend on learning—courses, books, conferences, or anything that supports your growth.

About the Team

Supabase was born-remote and open-source-first. We believe our globally distributed team is our secret weapon in building tools developers love.

  • ~400 team members

  • 60+ countries

  • 20+ languages spoken

  • Over $1B raised (including our $500M Series F)

  • 540,000+ community members

We move fast, build in public, and use what we ship. If it’s in your project, we probably use it in ours too. We believe deeply in the open-source ecosystem and strive to support—not replace—existing tools and communities.
